Aside from the typical shader compilation stutter that plague this game, this game manages to be an absolute disaster on a purely technical level.

The moment you pause or look at the main menu, the game engine forces your GPU to pull max wattage to live render heavy 3D assets behind the overlay. It completely drops frame gen, breaks the gsync hook and sends your gpu utilisation through the roof like a fcking stress test
i just watched it spend 15 minutes compiling shaders, crash, and then begin compiling shaders again, i think we genuinely do not hate Pitchford enough as a society

So after a thorough review of this game, I cannot recommend Shader Compiling Simulator for purchase. After spending more of my time compiling shaders than actually getting to play, I can confidently say that this game deserves nothing but the worst lol.

My playtime didn't even last two steps after laggy first cutscene. Played around 31 minutes? Nope. Most of that was Shader Compiling. I love Borderlands, but seriously? This isn't even a game, more of a slide show.

Starting the game for the first time looked like this:
19 minutes of compiling shaders.
4 times compiling shaders in total.
2 forced restarts.
1 crash.

The tutorial and intro section took 40 minutes to get through, before actually getting to the open world section, so an hour of total "playtime" before the game even started. 

It ran at a not-so-smooth 53 fps at the lowest settings with horrible frame times making everything feel horrible and look horrible and the frame gen could not save this. What I got to experience of the game is a dumb modern joke showering game that felt clunky and not like Borderlands at all. 

This game has totally lost itself and the optimization is non existing. It's such a shame to see Gearslop being this neglectful and greedy.

PLEASE SAVE YOUR MONEY and don't support this slop.

Open-world is take it or leave it, think the more condensed, bespoke maps of BL2 were preferred by me but YMMV. Dialogue is Borderlands lol, you know what you're signing up for. Usually I like to post reviews when I have either finished the game, or 100% the achievements but I felt like doing this one early because I am a huge fan of this series. I have a few positives and negatives from the time I have played so far that I wanted to speak my thoughts on.

The gameplay is REALLY fun, and easily the best in the series, the movement feels incredibly smooth and satisfying, the gun play is incredible, and the variety of guns is a treat. The abilities are super fun too, usually I am a hardcore siren main, through every single game, but the gameplay of Rafa in this is just far too much fun to pass on. The visuals are a really great update too and the map is huge, I also very much love the more serious tones of the story so far, whilst still keeping the classic borderlands humour.

The game is quite poorly optimised, albeit my PC is by no means good anymore and is outdated, I only get around 60fps on medium with full frame gen on, and some of my friends who have played on high end PCs have mentioned the optimisation is pretty poor. However this does seem to have improved significantly since launch.

My biggest issue is that the map, whilst being super big, feels really empty at times, especially if you are just driving to the next area, but this isn't a major concern I have really, still having a blast.

Definitely worth picking up and deserves much more love.

It’s more Borderlands, for better or worse. 

The excellent gunplay is still there, but without any innovation or twist, which renders the experience a bit stale for someone like me who has been playing since BL1.

The humor is no longer of the broccoli-head variety we saw with BL3, which is excellent, but it still lacks the dark wit of the Handsome Jack era. 

Unfortunately the news of abysmal performance is true. Performance as of June 2026 - coming up on a year after launch - is still unacceptably poor even with high end hardware. Worse yet, the game doesn’t even look better than BL3 - last gen graphics with current gen performance isssues.

They have added some movement stuff..because it can't be a new game without some sort of "Movement". There's a double jump, a dash, a ground pound and a BLATANTLY copied climbing mechanic from Apex Legends. I guess the changes are whatever.

Borderlands 4 Review: Somehow, the Loot Got Worse and So Did My Will to Live

Borderlands 4 is the kind of game that makes you stare at your controller and wonder if maybe going outside was the real endgame all along.

I wanted chaos. I wanted guns. I wanted stupid jokes, explosions, that classic Borderlands feeling of being rewarded every five seconds for having the attention span of a raccoon in a fireworks store. Instead, I got a game that feels like it was assembled by a committee of people who heard about Borderlands once during lunch. Also, WHY'D YOU TAKE AWAY DUELING??? Borderlands isn't Borderlands without not dueling your friends!!!

The humor tries so hard it should be issued a restraining order. Every character talks like they are auditioning for “Most Annoying Person in a Discord Server.” The jokes don’t land; they trip, fall down the stairs, then get back up to explain themselves for another three minutes. It's overly cringey AF...

The loot, somehow, is both overwhelming and boring. I picked up 700 solid guns AT THE BEGGINING OF THE GAME. It was a grind to get better guns in the earlier Borderland's games, now they just feed it to you like a baby...

The enemies are bullet sponges with legs. Shooting them feels less like combat and more like trying to kill a refrigerator with a Nerf gun. Boss fights are just health bars with emotional problems. You don’t beat them because you’re skilled. You beat them because eventually the game gets tired too.

The story? I genuinely do not know who this was for. It has the emotional depth of a gas station puddle. Characters show up, yell something “quirky,” disappear, then the game acts like I’m supposed to care. I have had stronger emotional connections with worn out sweatpants I wear during the winter then this garbage...

Visually, sure, it looks like Borderlands. But at this point that’s like saying a bad pizza still looks like pizza. It's a kick in the nuts to my taste buds and my taste for Borderlands.

Borderl…

Not impressed at all. Invisible walls, getting stuck after revive and dying all over again, strange hit detection, open world fatigue is already setting in with all the back tracking you have to do due to having to drag items back to base (you can't fast travel, you have to run all the way back). And I didn't think it was possible but it's even less funny than Borderlands 3 with worse characters. Regretting my purchase hard.

I don't really have complaints about the vault hunters, they're fun. I like the gun manufacturers and their gimmicks, I don't feel like I just use 1 or 2 manufacturers like in the 360 era games. The writing is what I expect from the post-marvel entertainment industry.
Also take heart AMD faithful, even I have to compile shaders regularly.

The shooting is still fun but otherwise it's very, very, very mediocre game.

The characters and especially the bad guys lack any depth and aren't even entertaining as a caricatures. Switching to the open world design also made most of the side missions feel very detached from the rest of the game and it's world. Even the main mission doesn't feel intense and the writing of the main character feels like lacking agency.

The open world concept just doesn't work in this particular game. It's like the devs haven't grasp what is the point of open word design or they have just thought it as a cheap and easy way to be able slap additional content later on. The open world map suffers a severe theme park syndrome. It is suppose to look like a vast world but it feel very crowded, everything being right next to each other. When there is a fast travel and an equipment to move faster than walking there isn't need to make a map that compact. The distance between places gives player time to breath. And despite the world filled with NPC and stuff it doesn't tempt player to explore since there is actually very little to find. 

The worst part is still that the game feels very unpolished. There are still many bugs, some which require you to restart the whole game and even occasional game crashes. Price tag sets expectation and game with price tag like this should have been more polished at least by now.

I went into this game with a clean slate not watching the trailers or anything of the matter and oh boy I wish I did.

The story is meh I suppose. The intro sequence didnt intice me or made me captivated to care. I chose RAFA since he seems to be one of the best vault hunters and honestly I dont like him. His knife blades are not for me, there a cool gimmick that I think would be fun if paired with more movent based abilities. 

The open world is bland and lack character. A smaller hand crafted world with a darker setting would work a lot better with the half assed humor its going for. The sidequest felt boring and a tad bit out of place in a borderlands game.

The guns are all the same. You have about 5 gun compagnies that offer a different way of shooting. You basically just choose a compagny that you like and stick with it. The diffrent guns are just the same guns with varied stats and perks.

I know I sound very negative about the game and if you think so I wouldnt blame you. The game itself still has a solid base and hopefully gearbox takes the feedback from the players and incorparates it into the next game. Knowing them tho I doubt it tho. 

I do think a borderlands MMO would be a great next step in the looter shooter genre.

5/10

Boarderlands should not be an open world game and this game shows why the Boarderlands franchise shines in segmented focused maps. When you make an open world game things naturally loose focus which for games with that in mind works. Boarderlands is a fast pass franchise where you want to get to the next location, the next level up, the next weapon farm, and so on. this game is drive over here kill these things drive over here talk to this guy drive over her kill these guys, and so on. Older BL's are like this but it's moving forward you're making progress to the next location here you already have access to everything other then the main bosses area.

             The idea of an open world Boarderlands was an interesting idea but just doesn't work you're put in a pretty uninteresting world with lots of nothing going on. With the same unfunny writing from BL3. I also think these are the most unintresting classes we've ever gotten I think all of the abilities a very boring but that's just me. If you play BL games already you probably already own this and lost interest if you've never played a BL game get 3 or 2 depending on if you want a newer or older experience if you pick 3 though find a guide to remove all the dialogue the game is much more playable that way.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires compiling shaders during startup and when changing graphics settings.

citations.review_text:
Terrible performance. It’s been almost a year since launch, and these issues still aren't fixed. It’s completely unacceptable.

The game forces you to wait for shaders to compile during the loading screen, and it does it again every time you try to change a graphics setting. It is incredibly frustrating, Randy Bitchford and his team can kiss my a**. They should be embarrassed.

My Verdict: Stay away from this one.

A third of the gameplay time is spent compiling shaders (the pattern is this: splash Screen, shader loading, game closes, Windows Powershell appears, second shader loading, launcher starts, third shader loading, hopefully the game starts). 

The other two-thirds are a poor imitation of Borderlands.

citations.review_text: The gameplay was fun.  I don't care about story so can't really comment on that.  The performance and crashes are unacceptable so long after release. It crashed at least once per hour. Frustrating way to play a great game.

It is impressive how this game has only performed worse with time.

citations.review_text: I mean, it's a Borderlands Game. They don't stray too far from the winning formula, but they mix it up enough that it's novel. please don't ever make an open world borderlands again.

You'll like this game if you've played any part of Borderlands before, and you'll love it even more if you're a fan of the entire series.

If you don't much care about controversial statements of Randy Pitchford, which caused a public outcry at the release, and the obviously inflated price tag (both for the main game and all DLCs), then in the first hours the impressions about the game itself are only good.

You can accelerate, make jumps, double jumps, dash, slide, cling to ledges, quickly use grappling hook, grab explosive objects and throw them, hit the ground with force, hover, climb walls, instantly summon transport and teleport into it and jump out of it just as instantly. All this creates an amazing entertainment experience and unique situations during battles and shootouts.

Whatever it is, upon the whole I mostly enjoyed the game, but wish that the devs would polish the technical part and reduce their appetites concerning DLCs price tags.

Like the game don't really like the performance but it has gotten better than what it was. Would love to see them  work on Migrating the game from UE5.3 to UE5.8 would solve Shader stutter and PSO handling and better CPU Parallelism & Multithreading Improvements

The game would be good if they would fix the optimization rather than just blaming the buyer's for not having a good enough PC.

citations.review_text: Extremally fun to play! Have had a few hicups here and there with crashes and corrupted data, but easily fixed once searching for help online! Definitely recommend to all who enjoy funny action packed games with unique graphical art!

I only bought this game because it was on sale, since around release time of this game, lots of users reporting poor graphics performance. Gave it a chance on my GTX 1080Ti (11GB) card. Not good, I had many crashes, even stupid ones, like on pause, or shopping for guns on the gun machine. I even had the power go out once on me and the saved game was corrupted so I had to start all over from a new game. I was on level 30 so a huge bummer there. My computer barely handles the game on lowest graphic setting, and motion is jumpy. 

I can't believe how bad performance is honestly. Just as a comparison, I played Borderlands 3 on my laptop just yesterday (it only has a 6GB Graphics card), and the gaming, motion is nice and smooth. Maybe it's something about the way developers built ONE GIANT MAP on BL4 that could be part of the issue, but I really think they dropped the ball on this release. They need to consult AI or something and get a patch out to help this issue. haha, I know I am wishful. I have never had this much trouble playing a game when I know my hardware is not basic.

Just when I thought things were about as rough as I could get with gameplay performance, I played today and it somehow got worse. I did notice the snowy mountainous area of the map does not handle as well as the other areas though. This is unplayable now, and I think I'm done fooling with this game. When people buy this game, I think it should come with a warning. Like "Recommended for higher-end gaming machines with 24gb GFX cards or better."

Now for my take on the game designs and characters. I am excellent with reading and recognizing voices so you will notice I have more opinion than most on this. I think Gearbox needs to work on their NPC's and get better voice actors that have more personality. Additionally, this game was only mildly humorous, and to me the humor has faded ever since BL1. Eve…

With the most recent patch, the game opens, verifies there's a patch, then goes into a death boot loop where it says it sees the patches and then on game reboot, the OakGame thing fails and says "fatal error". I have verified the files, uninstalled, and reinstalled the game to no avail.

[UPDATE] I believe there was an issue with the AMD Radeon driver, but I am uncertain if it was a setting or it initialized improperly. Now that the game is running properly again, it is enjoyable with some good mechanics, but not as funny as the prior installments and the score seems to be a bit diminished this time around. So long as the launcher works then I am fine with recommending the game.

Borderlands 4 has moments of solid combat and entertaining loot, but they are buried under poor quest design, poor plotting, poor characters and a remarkable number of bugs. I encountered broken objectives, missing markers, unreliable item effects, awkward carry quests, disappearing map icons, and crashes to name just a few of the problems.

I am approximately 50% through the game, and, while I have had crashes and start up issues before, it will now no longer start.  Every launch ends on a black screen with the render thread hanging. Today, a year after the game was first released, Borderlands 4 is still too buggy to play reliably.

If you are going to buy this game don't do it yet. It is unplayable due to bugs.

Game still runs horrible, constant stutters and trying to download shaders. I've done every recommended fix and I am still crashing every 5-10 minutes.
The game would be good if they would fix the optimization rather than just blaming the buyer's for not having a good enough PC.

However, this one is unique in that: The open world makes it especially bad. Instead of making missions and side-quests more complex or interesting, every SINGLE task requires the player to travel some inane distance in the effort of making these missions SEEM longer.
This barely feels like a Borderlands game, and the writers knew that, so they shoe-horned in some beloved characters and called it a day. 
Whats good? The gameplay: It features everything ALL videogames apparently need:  shooting, jumping, double jumping, gliding, sliding, dodging, AND over-extended ability trees!

The story telling, the characters, the main nemesis and the irony are all at elementary school level. The world does not feel ''open'' at all. The performance is completely offensive. After the main story, there is nothing to do, apart from repeating boss runs until nausea hits you. This game is completely bankrupt, creatively. It is a big ball of banality, just like BDL3. A pointless product that leaves nothing to the player, made by a studio that doesn't have anything to say anymore.

I've been playing Borderlands for about 15 years. I have thousands of hours across Borderlands 2 & 3 and 100s across each non-mainline entry. But after 500 hours in Borderlands 4 and I still dont know where I stand on it entirely. So I'll break it all down into key peices, and let the story tell itself.

:Gameplay & World:
Gunplay and exploration is the cleanest the series has felt so far. Adding to the Mantle & Slide introduced in BL3, Glide & Grapple are the new additions. Kairos feels both wider and taller and traversal feels unique. Kairos makes great use of your movement set, having chests and collectables across large caverns allows you to make use of the glide and having grapple points littered through the world allows for quick escapes from combat. Enemy design is great. Enemies are super responsive, they take cover and flank and some of the new designs feel unique to Kairos. Some enemies come with modifiers, akin to BL3's mayhem modifiers, but the enemies that do are few and far between so modifiers are less a "difficulty spiking" mechanic, and more an occasional gameplay variation. SDU progression has been tied to in-world activities and collectibles, so unfortunately new character runs feel tedious & repetitive when you've already explored the entirety of Kairos 3 times already for the exact same collectibles - just to increase your ammo caps and backpack space.

I dont think Borderlands 4 explicitly needed to go open world. This game would not have suffered from the previous games level design. The 3 main biomes each have 3 or 4 segments, and these would have been perfectly fine as thier own maps. As tedious to navigate as it is, I think Carcadia Burn certainly would have benefited from being broken down into smaller chunks. Your inventory is now an entire screen-spanning menu, rather than previous games more "in-world" approach.

:Loot & Bosses:
Loot & drop rates are in the best place they've been since BL2. Legendary world drops now feel rare c…

This game has something in common with modern CODs. It's lost its soul. It's lost the charm that made it so magical back in the day. The map design is pretty meh as it was given the Ubisoft open world slop treatment. That being said, there are many positives. I'd argue more positives than negatives. This game is a big step up from borderlands 3 in every way except the world design. It plays great. The movement and gunplay are the best they have ever been. The skills trees and characters are the best they've ever been. Overall I love this game and it's my favorite entry in the series by a pretty wide margin. I just hope one day they can re-capture that spark that created this absolute juggernaut of a looter shooter.

Overall I'm gonna give this game a solid 7.5

Got it on sale and was still disappointed. Its better than 3, worse than 2, story wise (what the hell even happened in BL3 its so unmemorable), but preforms like total ♥♥♥♥ comparatively. Its a facade of an open world game. I have no idea why they haven't been able to figure out how to make a properly open world game in the current era. Probably laziness. As a fan of the series I had some enjoyable moments but not nearly enough to outweigh my gripes. If they cant figure it out before BL5 I hope they let the series die after this one. If you intend to purchase wait for Gearbox to release all the content they intend to release for it, and then wait for a Steam sale to get it at a steep discount.

You'll like this game if you've played any part of Borderlands before, and you'll love it even more if you're a fan of the entire series.

If you don't much care about controversial statements of Randy Pitchford, which caused a public outcry at the release, and the obviously inflated price tag (both for the main game and all DLCs), then in the first hours the impressions about the game itself are only good.

This is definitely one of the most dynamic first-person shooters, where I experienced incredible freedom and convenience in terms of flexible character control. You can accelerate, make jumps, double jumps, dash, slide, cling to ledges, quickly use grappling hook, grab explosive objects and throw them, hit the ground with force, hover, climb walls, instantly summon transport and teleport into it and jump out of it just as instantly. All this creates an amazing entertainment experience and unique situations during battles and shootouts.

The main storyline is straightforward and simple, but some of the side-missions are made more creative and interesting with typical Borderlands humour. Open world is definitely overwhelmed with activities and collectibles, but they're easily skippable If you're bored to find them all.

I've not faced any critical errors during the whole walkthrough, but optimization is still leaves much to be desired. So "compiling shaders" simulator is not a joke, but a constant part of the game... and that's sad.

Whatever it is, upon the whole I mostly enjoyed the game, but wish that the devs would polish the technical part and reduce their appetites concerning DLCs price tags.

The game is much better (fuller) than it was on its initial release. It's probably that I wasn't paying attention first play through, but there's more environment, animals, sounds, effects, in the game now that last August '25. The only criticism I'd make is the DLCs are really crap, and not worth the cost, maybe at$5 each, but not at $25+

The pricing of this game and expansions is silly. As someone who bought the base game previously, It would be more expensive for me to purchase the Vault Hunter Pack + Bounty Pack then it would be to just purchase the "Super Deluxe Edition." I think it is silly that I would effectively be rebuying the game to get the DLC bundled at a lower price than buying them separately. This is probably to boost their low sales numbers but I am not going to take part in this until their DLC is properly on sale.

Summer Sale Example: Base Edition $35 + Vault Hunter Pack $50 + Bounty Pack $40 = $125 USD
Super Deluxe Edition (Base Edition, Vault Hunter Pack, Bounty Pack included) = $65 USD

But why should I have to buy a new edition to get the DLC at an affordable price? I already own the base game.
